title: HMAC C_Verify branch after volatile XOR loop is not constant-time
description:
In wp11_pkcs11.c around line 6003, HMAC verification uses a volatile XOR accumulator loop followed by 'if (diff != 0)'. The branch leaks timing information: a compiler is free to optimize the volatile loop away or introduce branch misprediction observable via cache timing. wolfCrypt provides wc_ConstantCompare() (or XMEMCMP_CT). The branch-after-loop pattern is the classic mistake in hand-rolled constant-time compares.

Fix: replace the volatile XOR loop with wc_ConstantCompare() or equivalent from wolfCrypt. Add comment explaining why a library function is required rather than rolling our own.
